title.narrative: (Consortium) Strengthening Food Security and Resilience through Integrated FSL, Health, Nutrition, WASH, and Protection Services in Conflict-Affected Areas of Nyala Shimal Nyala Janoub, South Darfur

description.narrative: ltpgtThis integrated multi-sectoral project, led by ALIGHT in partnership with JMCO, NIDO, and World Vision International (WVI), targets critical humanitarian needs in Nyala Shimal and Nyala Janoub localities of South Darfur. Funded through the 2025 Sudan Humanitarian Fund (SHF) Standard Allocation, this 12-month project aims to reach vulnerable internally displaced persons (IDPs) and host communities affected by conflict, displacement, food insecurity, disease outbreaks, and the collapse of basic services. It aligns with the Humanitarian Response Plan Strategic Objectives 1 and 3 by delivering lifesaving assistance and restoring access to essential services.ltbrgtIn Health, the project will support five health facilities: two Primary Health Care Centers managed by ALIGHT in Nyala Janoub and three Primary Health Units managed by WVI in Nyala Shimal. It aims to deliver 72,244 outpatient consultations, including 1,050 safe births, 960 mental health consultations, and 1,800 routine immunizations. Support will include medical supply distribution, disease surveillance, and outbreak response. To ensure inclusion, the project will enhance accessibility for persons with disabilities through facility upgrades such as ramps, handrails, and accessible toilets.ltbrgtIn Nutrition, 134,567 individuals will benefit through five targeted sites. Planned interventions include MUAC screening for 29,000 individuals, treatment of 1,550 moderate acute malnutrition (MAM) cases, 1,461 severe acute malnutrition (SAM) cases, and referral of 230 SAM cases with complications. Additionally, 950 caregivers will receive Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) counseling, and 12 mother support groups will be formed to promote community-based care practices.ltbrgtThe Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL) component will support household recovery and reduce dependency on negative coping mechanisms. The project will provide agricultural kits to 400 households, restock 800 goats to benefit 200 female-headed households, and vaccinate or treat 20,000 livestock. It will also distribute 200 donkey carts and ploughs and train 100 farmers in climate-resilient agriculture practices to strengthen livelihoods and enhance food production.ltbrgtIn WASH, the project will rehabilitate two water yards in Nyala Shimal to improve access to safe water for 15,000 people. Water quality monitoring and training of 30 water committee members will be conducted to ensure long-term functionality. Hygiene promotion will reach 15,000 people through 12 clean-up campaigns, 60 trained hygiene promoters, and the distribution of 400 hygiene kits.ltbrgtUnder Protection, the project will deliver GBV case management and MHPSS for 200 survivors, train 30 GBV service providers, and distribute 600 dignity kits. In Child Protection, 150 children will receive case management and MHPSS support. Two community-based child protection networks will be established, and one Child-Friendly Space will be rehabilitated to benefit 400 children. General Protection efforts include 12 monthly monitoring visits, awareness campaigns for 11,190 people, training of 60 humanitarian workers on PSEA, and support to two local protection committees.ltbrgtThe Emergency Response and Rapid Mechanism (ERRM) contingency budget line allows timely response to needs arising from new displacement, especially from Zamzam, including areas in and around Jabal Marra. Activities may be implemented anywhere in the project area but must be directly related to the crisis. Concept notes will follow the SHF 48-hour response template and, once approved, must be launched immediately.ltbrgtGiven the high levels of displacement, IPC Phase 5 famine risk, ongoing conflict, and weak health and WASH systems, this project is urgently needed. It will save lives, restore dignity, and support inclusive, community-led recovery in South Darfur.ltbrgtlt/pgt
